This small plot is my enset and a few coffee trees near the house, the land my husband and I planted long ago. I am old now and my hands are slow, but enset does not ask for much — I spread the cattle manure from our kraal around the base like my mother taught me, and that is enough. I have no money for the white fertilizer from the cooperative, and anyway my neighbors do not put it on their enset. The rain comes when it comes, and I carry water from the spring only for the youngest suckers when the dry months are hard.
